authority_binding_findings.title: Runtime H6 execution gate is bound to the SUPERSEDED, FAILED V1 preregistration
authority_binding_findings.consequences_fail_closed: Any legitimate V3 external-verification report records prereg_commit=9f1d844, spec_sha256=cd354e06…, manifest_sha256=de42e4a1…. _verify_external_report() would raise H6PreregMismatch, so can_execute_h6() can never return True through the legitimate path. The gate's enablement condition is not reachable for the live frozen authority.
authority_binding_findings.consequences_governance: Conversely, a report carrying the V1 hashes with FINAL_VERDICT=PASS at the V1 path would satisfy the gate while the live frozen authority is V3 — binding the runtime release decision to a preregistration that FAILED external verification and was superseded. Observed state today is fail-closed because no V1 report is present.
authority_binding_findings.verifier_action: REPORTED ONLY. Not repaired, per audit independence rules.

authority_binding_findings.title: External verifier report path is relative and CWD-dependent

evidence.note: A relative module-level Path resolves against the process working directory, so can_execute_h6() can differ between invocations depending on CWD, and can be satisfied by a file outside the audited worktree.

consistency_checks.note: src/trading_bot/research/h6/__init__.py still documents 'Frozen authority: H6_SPEC.json (committed blob e683e04) …' i.e. V1, while the frozen authority is V3.

verdict_summary: The data-plane artifacts are fully self-consistent and hash-verified; the CONTROL plane (runtime execution gate + package docstring) is still bound to the V1 preregistration. Currently fail-closed in practice, but the authority binding is wrong.
